source.caption:
Today I finished my last patient visit at my current clinic.

This was my first real job out of grad school, and the first job I’ve ever chosen to leave. Every job transition before this one just happened. Graduating high school, graduating college. The mentors I have I still work with to this day. This one felt different because I made the choice.

I looked back at the numbers from the past eighteen months. Over 4,000 patient visits. 319 unique cases. That’s a lot of humans. A lot of stories. A lot of hands-on problem-solving compressed into a short stretch of time.

Formal education cannot do what the clinic does. The practicality and skill development that come from repetition, from sitting with real people and real pain and real complexity, is unrivaled. No textbook replicates what happens when someone walks through the door hurting and trusts you to help them figure it out.

It’s bittersweet. But mostly I just feel grateful. Grateful for the mentors. Grateful for the staff. Grateful for every single patient who let me into their care over the last year and a half.

Time to write the next chapter.

Be Good.
Help Someone.
Learn Lots.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
